- Minimum load cell resistance: 43,8 Ω → 43.8 Ω
- Maximum load cell resistance: 1050 Ω
- Temperature range: -10 °C / +40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40}, °C
- Fraction of the maximum permissible error: 0,5 → 0.5
- Load cell connection: 6-wire (remote sensing)
- Max cable length per cross wire section: text — "No special cable length has to be provided..." — this is a descriptive value; can keep as string.

- Software identification: Version number: v0.1 → software identification value "v0.1" or software_version: v0.1

Since accuracy class varies as an axis, the varying attribute (max verification scale intervals) should go into config_level with axis "accuracy_class". Per rule 5: config_level with axis. The values: condition "class III" → 3000, condition "class IIII" → 1000. Value "n ≤ 3000" — the attribute is "maximum number of verification scale intervals" (n), so value is max 3000 → {min: null, max: 3000}? The "≤" indicates upper limit. Structured value: {min: null, max: 3000}. Unit: intervals — dimensionless; unit_symbol null.

Accuracy class itself is type_level? It's multiple values. Could represent as type_level attribute "accuracy_classes" with value list... but rules say lists of values are model matrices. Hmm. Accuracy classes are captured in recommendation.accuracy_classes. I could also do config_level for class-dependent attributes only.

Canonical label: maximum_cable_length_per_cross_wire_section — hmm, maybe "cable_length_requirement". Let's use "maximum_cable_length_cross_wire_section" with value as string.
- weighing_ranges: "Single interval"
- software_version: "v0.1"

Actually the structured value format for config_level: `{condition, value, unit_symbol}`. The value itself is number or range object? In type_level, values are {value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers}. In config_level, values follow same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. So value: {min: null, max: 3000}? Or just 3000 since "n ≤ 3000" means maximum is 3000 — value is the max number of intervals, so value: 3000 with the ≤ being implicit in the attribute being "maximum". I think value: 3000 plainly is fine — the attribute name already says "maximum". Yes, better: value: 3000.

No model family — single model DIS1000. Could include model_family only if >1 model variant; only one model, so omit.

Matrix tables: the characteristics table fits into type_level + config_level, so no matrix_tables needed. I could skip matrix_tables.
